images.filename: Burke River anabranch channel Boulia Queensland P1030234bd.jpg
images.caption: The Burke River is an ephemeral, desert river in central western Queensland.  It is part of the Lake Eyre basin. The river was named in memory of explorer Robert O'Hara Burke of the Burke and Wills expedition.  The Burke River rises in the Selwyn Range north of Boulia. It flows south past Boulia until it discharges into the Georgina River.  As one of the Channel Country rivers it has multiple anabranches on its broad floodplain.  Iconic river red gums (Eucalyptus camaldulensis) and coolabah (Eucalyptus coolabah) line the banks, with coolabah also found on the floodplain.

images.filename: Boulia Turf Club Selwyn Rd flooded by Burke River March 2019 Boulia Queensland - photo Anna Kara.jpg
images.caption: Tropical Cyclone Trevor brought heavy rain to Boulia Shire in March 2019.  The Burke River spread across its flood plain, inundating the Boulia Turf Club.
images.alt: Tropical Cyclone Trevor brought heavy rain to Boulia Shire in March 2019.  The Burke River spread across its flood plain, inundating the Boulia Turf Club.

images.filename: Boulia Roadhouse and Diamantina Developmental Rd flooded by Burke River March 2019, Boulia Queensland - photo Anna Kara.jpg
images.caption: Tropical Cyclone Trevor brought heavy rain to Boulia Shire in March 2019.  Flood waters of the Burke River reached the outskirts of Boulia and cut the Diamantina Developmental Rd.
